description: Live end-to-end analysis of an encrypted network capture: container probe, byte features, dissector identification, bounded recovery, flow features, behavior rules, conditional classification and evidence report.
limitations: M03-M06 (unknown-structure inference) are deliberately not selected: these captures are already identified standard protocols, and framing the pcap container bytes as application messages would be meaningless rather than informative.
M02 windows are 16384 bytes so that byte-distribution profiles stay bounded on multi-megabyte captures.
M08 runs on the longest reassembled direction with the TLS record layout declared; if that direction does not tile under the declared layout, M08 keeps the whole-input refusal instead of a recovery.

Both samples here do tile: the VPN capture's longest direction is a mid-session TLS stream to port 443 with no handshake in view, so only record headers are recovered there, while the direct TLS 1.3 capture also yields a plaintext ServerHello.
Only regions RFC 8446 declares unprotected are recovered; protected bytes are refused and counted. Which regions those are is declared to M08, not inferred.
The reused M11 classifier was trained on controlled HTTP captures; predictions over external encrypted flows are demonstrative and are not a generalization claim.
